document_title: Petersburg's Three Data Center Tests, and the Wider Freeze

slides.headline:
Petersburg drafted three data center tests.
Then it widened the freeze.
labels: SCHEMATIC MODULE, NOT A REAL PROJECT

slides.headline:
5 to 2 to cover all data centers.
Then 7 to 0.
slides.body: The amendment would widen the freeze to every data center, on or off the grid, whatever its cooling. The Petersburg Pilot says it closes the opening left for Mazzella's 2-megawatt project. The final reading is scheduled for November 30th at 6 p.m.
labels: AS REPORTED · REVISED TEXT NOT YET PUBLISHED

slides.headline: The grid, in writing.
slides.body: No permit unless Petersburg Municipal Power & Light found, in writing, that today's grid could fully supply the load.
labels: A NUMBER ONLY THE UTILITY CAN WRITE

slides.headline:
No generators
for everyday power.
slides.body: Diesel, gas or any generator was barred as everyday power. Backup during a real outage, or a curtailment the utility directs, was allowed.
labels: "none of us wants generators running 24/7, and that's the purpose of this ordinance"
STEVE HARBOUR, UTILITY DIRECTOR, WHO HELPED WRITE IT
BACKUP ONLY · OUTAGE OR PMPL CURTAILMENT

slides.headline: Every drop of coolant stays in the loop.
slides.body: 100 percent of coolant and refrigerant circuits had to stay contained and keep recirculating. An Alaska-licensed engineer had to certify the cooling plans.

slides.headline: As of mid-November, Petersburg had no data centers.
labels: PER KFSK · THE TOWN RUNS ON HYDROPOWER, MOSTLY BOUGHT FROM SEAPA
SO WHY FREEZE ALL OF THEM? THE VOTES ARE NEXT.

slides.headline: The same amendment tied, then passed.
slides.body: Mayor Bob Lynn and Stanton Gregor voted no on the amendment.
labels: NOVEMBER 2ND · FIRST READING · 5 TO 1 · ONE EXCUSED
JEFF MEUCCI, WHO MOVED THE AMENDMENT
"a solution in search of a problem"

ON ADOPTION · IN EFFECT, PENDING APPLICATIONS INCLUDED
PERMITS ISSUED BEFORE ADOPTION ARE NOT REVOKED
JUNE 21ST, 2027 · FINDINGS DUE TO THE ASSEMBLY

slides.headline: Should the final text keep the three tests for when the freeze ends?

post_copy:
On November 2nd, Petersburg's draft data center freeze had three tests. On November 16th, a 5 to 2 vote widened it to every data center.

Three drafted tests, five Assembly tallies and the clock to 2027.

The tests were exact. The utility had to confirm in writing that today's grid could fully supply the load. No generators for everyday power. Coolant had to stay 100 percent in the loop.

Jeff Meucci's amendment tied 3 to 3 on November 2nd and passed two weeks later. The Petersburg Pilot says it closes the opening left for Mazzella's 2-megawatt project.

As of mid-November, Petersburg had no data centers. The final vote is scheduled for November 30th. A full pause is defensible.

The tests are worth keeping. If the freeze ends on September 30th, 2027, should they become the rules, or should Petersburg start over?

#PetersburgAK #DataCenterPolicy #SoutheastAlaska
